findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Observed TCS foods not being cold held below 41 F in a broken prep cooler. CORRECTED: PIC and staff discarded TCS food items that were inside the prep cooler if they were prepared longer than 4 hours ago, and TCS items prepared under 4 hours were moved to a working cooler. This cooler cannot be used for service unless it is repaired (see Violation #33) or a Time as Control Policy is created and used. Ensure that TCS foods are maintained at temperatures of 41 F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Observed that the prep cooler on the far end of the kitchen by the office was still observed not keeping the appropriate temperature range. The average temperature within the cooler using the infrared thermometer was 55F. Temperatures obtained by probing was 45F. PICs previously told Inspector that the unit will be repaired accordingly, but per PICs they are still waiting on a part. Cease using the prep cooler for cold holding until it is repaired. Ensure that the necessary repairs are done enabling the unit to have the appropriate temperature capacity.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use.
findings.comment: An open employee drink was observed sitting on the chopping surface of the prep cooler on the cook line. Education was carried out. The drink was removed. Ensure that employees are remember to have a lid on their drinks and stored in a place the helps prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-401.11(B) Eating, Drinking, or Using TOBACCO PRODUCTS.(B) A FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from a closed BEVERAGE container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: (1) The EMPLOYEE'S hands; (2) The container; and (3) Exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Employees were observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was provided and the behavior was corrected.  Ensure that employees are reminded to always properly wash their hands before donning gloves in between tasks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: REPEAT: Inspector observed multiple cans of ripe olives dented along the seams. CORRECTED- the PIC removed the cans from service to be returned to the supplier. Ensure cans are frequently checked for dents along the seams to prevent the entry and harborage of Botulism.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed both bar soda nozzles and soda gun holders to be soiled. CORRECTED- Employees cleaned and sanitized the food contact surfaces. Ensure soda nozzles and the soda gun holder are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation. Food contact surfaces must be clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
REPEAT x2: The following were observed. 
1. Inspector observed 2 sanitizer buckets to be between 0-100 ppm of quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- buckets were remade at a proper concentration (200 ppm). 
2. The sanitizer concentration in the dish machine was observed reading opposite for chlorine. CORRECTED- The EcoLab technician was called and the dish machine was repaired at the end of the inspection.
 Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at frequency to maintain the sanitizer concentration as recommended by the manufacturer's label including frequently checking the sanitizer concentration within the dish machine.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: The prep cooler on the far end of the kitchen by the office was observed not keeping the appropriate temperature range. A discussion was held about the appropriate action needed. The average temperature within the cooler using the infrared thermometer was 55F. Temperatures obtained by probing was 44F. The food items were removed to a different unit. The PIC told inspector that the unit will be repaired accordingly. Ensure that teh necessary repairs are done enabling the unit to have the appropriate temperature capacity.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Multiple boxes of food items which includes but not limited to grilled chicken and hame were observed being stored on the floor in both the walk-in cooler and the walk-in freezer. Discussed with the PIC. The items were removed to be stored appropriately. Ensure that food items are stored at least six inches above the cooler to avoid exposure to splash or other contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the door between the walk in cooler and walk in freezer to contain a sizable gap, and the gaskets to be loose. The PIC stated a new frame is being ordered. Ensure the door is repaired or replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(B) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (B) EQUIPMENT components such as doors, seals, hinges, fasteners, and kick plates shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted in accordance with manufacturer's specifications. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: FOURTH REPEAT: The wire shelving on the far right corner by the entrance of the walk-in freezer in the walk in cooler is soiled and rusted. Inspector discussed getting shelf liners, cleaning/ painting, or replacing shelves. One large green shelf was replaced and the other cleaned. The PIC stated they will be ordering new shelving. Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The hood baffles and fire suppression system were observed to contain an accumulation of grease drips and debris. Grease drips pose a threat of contamination to ready to eat (RTE) foods, and can serve as a fire hazard. Ensure the hood vent system and baffles are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: An accumulation of grease, soil, and food debris was observed under the fryers. The PIC was made aware. The PIC assured inspector that they do get accumulation buildup will be cleaned. Ensure that the accumulation is cleaned providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The mop head was observed stored improperly in the mop bucket. The PIC was made aware. Ensure that mop heads are stored in a way that allows them to air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspectors observed uncut avocado sitting directly on top of raw shelled eggs in the cook line prep cooler. CORRECTED- the avocado was moved into a separate container, and the eggs were moved below. Ensure raw animal proteins are kept separate from ready to eat (RTE) food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Multiple food contact items were observed to contain an accumulation of debris during today’s inspection:
1) FIRST REPEAT: A knife on the magnetic strip next to the salad prep station. CORRECTED: The knife was brought to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
2)  FIRST REPEAT: The ice baffle on the North ice machine was observed to contain a slight accumulation of debris. The PIC stated the machine was serviced 3 days ago. CORRECTED- overall cleaning of the ice baffles has improved. PIC stated the machines will be cleaned at an increased frequency.
3) Vegetable chopper contained food debris in the upper portion of the equipment. CORRECTED- equipment was brought to the dish area to be cleaned and sanitized.
Ensure all food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight and touch to prevent contamination of RTE foods.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspector observed 3 sanitizer buckets to be between 0-100 ppm of quaternary ammonia. CORRECTED- buckets were remade at a proper concentration (200-400 ppm). Ensure sanitizer buckets are made at frequency to maintain the sanitizer concentration as recommended by the manufacterer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.[P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed multiple items to be held past their seven day date mark (gyro meat- 10/31, salsa ranch- 10/27, and chipotle BBQ-10/27). CORRECTED- the gyro meat was discarded, and the PIC stated the other sauces had been remade since the sticker date, and the items were re-stickered with the correct dates. Ensure all Time/Temperature Control for Food Safety (TCS) food items are marked with the date they are prepared, and are used or discarded within seven days. The day of preparation or thawing counts as day one. To help ensure this practice takes place, ensure sauces are placed into a new container that has been clean and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed insect stun light above single service articles at the entry of the kitchen. Ensure that insect control devices are stored away from single service items to prevent contamination of food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored.
findings.comment: There were multiple wiping cloths that were observed to be stored on the counter in between uses, rather than being stored in the sanitizer bucket. This was discussed with the PIC. Ensure that wiping cloths are stored in the sanitizer bucket in between uses to prevent bacterial growth on the cloths.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.14(B) Wiping Cloths, Use Limitation. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be: (1) Held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution at a concentration specified under § 4-501.114; and (2) Laundered daily as specified under 4-802.11(D).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Multiple nonfood contact surfaces were observed to contain an accumulation of debris:
1) The top of the dish machine contains a layer of debris.
2) The shelf liners in the dry storage contained an accumulation of dust.
3) SECOND REPEAT: The wire shelving in the walk in cooler is soiled and rusted. Inspector discussed getting shelf liners, cleaning/ painting, or replacing shelves.
4) SECOND REPEAT: The shelving on the cook line contains an accumulation of dust. 
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation or dust or debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Multiple physical facilities were observed to be in need of repair:
1) THIRD REPEAT: The triple sink and table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked.
2) FIRST REPEAT: The hand sink in the south men’s bathroom was not adhered to the wall. There is also not a large enough gap to easily clean between the sink and the wall. The sink should be sealed to the wall to be smooth and easily cleanable.
Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: The PIC stated their Allergen Awareness Certificate had expired, and they were unable to produce Allergen Awareness certificates for any Certified Food Protection Managers (CFM/CFPM). Inspector provided Allergen Awareness literature to the PIC, which included a web address to ANSI-accredited institutes. Ensure all CFMs obtain an Allergen Awareness certificate. 

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the hand sink at the bar being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- employee moved the dump tray to the triple sink. Ensure that hand washing sinks are being used for hand washing only.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw meat was observed to be stored on top of a ranch container in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- PIC moved the raw meat beneath the ranch. Ensure that raw food is stored beneath ready-to-eat food.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables. [P]

2) Knives on the magnetic strip in the kitchen were observed to contain food debris. CORRECTED- person in charge moved the knives to be cleaned and sanitized. All food contact surfaces that will be used on ready-to-eat foods must be clean to sight and touch.
3) Magnetic strip for the knives contained grease and debris. Non-food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch. A follow up inspection will occur on 07/28/25 to ensure that the knife strip are cleaned or sanitized.

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature.
findings.comment: Inspector observed chicken cooling in the walk in freezer to be stacked in a tub. Education occurred with the person in charge regarding the need for shallow pans for food to have the surface area to properly cool. In it’s current configuration the chicken will not reach cooling temperature benchmarks in the required time.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.14(A) Cooling. (A) Cooked time/temperature control for safety food shall be cooled: (1) Within 2 hours from 57C (135F) to 21C (70°F); and (2) Within a total of 6 hours from 57C (135F) to 5C (41°F) or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Lime juice and whipping cream located at the bar reach in cooler did not have date marking. CORRECTED- Education occurred about date marking and dates were placed on the whipping cream and lime juice. Ensure items being held for more than 24 hours are marked with the date the container was opened, so that they may be used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded, based on the temperature and time combinations specified in (A) of this section and: (1) The day the original container is opened in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be counted as Day 1; and (2) The day or date marked by the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on FOOD safety. [Pf]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed insect stun light above single service articles at the entry of the kitchen. Ensure that insect control devices are stored away from single service items to prevent contamination.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Inspector observed chicken bouillon with an open lid to be located on the floor of the dry storage area. All food items should remain covered when not in use, and must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor to protect items from contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
1) FIRST REPEAT- Wire shelving in the walk-in cooler is soiled or rusted (straight across from the door and to the left when you walk in the cooler). Wire shelving over the prep counter (above the under-counter freezer) is dusty. Clean dusty/dirty shelves. Replace rusted shelves that are no longer smooth/easily cleanable.
2)  Significant amounts of food debris were observed on the floors in the walk in freezer and throughout the kitchen. 
3) The floors of the walk-in freezer and bar walk-in cooler were wet from the cooling system dripping.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1) 2nd REPEAT: The triple sink and table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked.
2) 1st REPEAT: There are holes in the wall above the hand-sink and the triple sink that need caulked.
3) 1st REPEAT: The kitchen handwashing sink needs re-caulked.
4) A hole was observed in the east wall of the dry storage above the water heater.
5) The hand sink in the south men’s bathroom was not adhered to the wall. There is also not a large enough gap to easily clean between the sink and the wall. The sink should be sealed to the wall to be smooth and easily cleanable.
6) Both walk-in coolers appeared to be dripping water from their compressors (see violation #49). The bar walk in cooler contained several ready-to-eat items, including cut fruit, red peppers flakes, parmesan cheese, and milk. This provides an opportunity for cross contamination. 

Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
The CFM was unable to show inspectors allergen awareness training certificate. All CFMs must obtain allergen awareness training within 30 days of employment. Inspector gave allergen certification information to the CFM.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: No paper towels were available at the bar handwashing sink. CORRECTED- Employees provided a roll of paper towels to keep at the handsink. Ensure paper towels are always available at all handwashing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Both bar soda nozzles were observed to be soiled. CORRECTED- Employees cleaned the soda nozzles. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11 (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Drain cleaner and window cleaner were observed stored among drink mixes and alcohol under the bar. A can of Pledge was observed stored among condiments and over cups and paper-wrapped straws at the north wait station. CORRECTED- Chemicals were removed to be stored away from food, utensils, and single-service articles.
findings.citation_text: 7-201.11 Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Wire shelving in the walk-in cooler is soiled or rusted (straight across from the door and to the left when you walk in the cooler). Wire shelving over the prep counter (above the under-counter freezer) is dusty. Clean dusty/dirty shelves. Replace rusted shelves that are no longer smooth/easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: 1) The triple sink and table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked. Cease use of black caulk in the kitchen/dish areas as it will hide soil accumulation.
2) There are holes in the wall above the handsink and the triple sink that need caulked.
3) The kitchen handwashing sink needs re-caulked.
Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: Employee coats were observed stored hanging on dry storage shelves. Designate areas away from food/single service items for the storage of employees personal items.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.110 (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Multiple employees were observed to wash their hands without utilizing a barrier to turn the faucet off. Ensure that handwashing is reviewed with all employees. To avoid recontaminating the hands, it is important that a barrier is used to turn off the faucet. CORRECTED- The employees were educated on proper handwashing. 

 (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There were raw eggs stored above cheese and other RTE foods in the walk-in cooler. CORRECTED- These eggs were moved to the bottom shelf. Ensure that raw eggs are stored below RTE foods. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The ice baffle and the right bar soda nozzle were observed to have accumulation of soil residue on them. CORRECTED- These items were cleaned during the inspection. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: The temperature of foods, including pizza sauce, cheese, and sausage, were probed to be between 46F and 52F in the top of the left prep cooler across from the cook line. CORRECTED- The items in this cooler were all placed in an ice bath, due to the cooler not holding foods at 41F and below. The food had only been in there two hours when the temperature was found to be above the 41F. Ensure that all TCS food is held at 41F or below. 

There was chicken in an ice bath in the kitchen that was probed to be at 46F. The ice bath was not full and was only touching the bottom of the pans. Ensure that when keeping TCS food in an ice bath that the ice bath is submerging the bottom pan enough to keep it below 41F. CORRECTED- The ice bath was filled to allow the bottom of the pans to be submerged in the ice bath. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: The left prep cooler in the kitchen across from the cook line was observed to be holding at above 41F. The foods in this cooler were probed to be between 46F and 52F. The food items in the cooler were placed in an ice bath. A follow up will be conducted on 9/27/2024 to ensure that the prep cooler has been repaired and is holding foods at 41F or below. 

EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There were multiple wiping cloths that were observed to be stored on surfaces in between uses. Ensure that cloths that are in use for wiping counters and equipment surfaces should be held in a chemical sanitizer at the proper solution if not currently in use. 

(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: There is a leak observed coming from both of the bar faucets and the triple sink faucet. Ensure that these leaks are repaired by next routine inspection. Plumbing systems should be maintained in good repair. 

A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The following physical facilities were observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The triple sink and the table to the right of the dish machine need re-caulked. 
2. There are holes in the wall above the handwashing sink and the triple sink that need caulked. 
3. The kitchen handwashing sink needs re-caulked. 

Ensure that all of these physical facilities are repaired and are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1) The kitchen handsink was blocked by a colander of black beans stored in its basin at the beginning of the inspection. CORRECTED- An employee removed the beans and colander from the sink.
2) An employee placed a sanitizer bucket in the basin of the handsink. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was removed from the basin of the handsink.
Keep handsinks clear and accessible at all times. Handsinks are only to be used for handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. [Pf]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket at the north wait station and the sanitize compartment of the bar triple sink were observed with 100ppm quat. CORRECTED- Sanitizer bucket was remade. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Containers of chili and alfredo sauce were observed cooling in the walk-in cooler with no additional cooling methods used. Both were at or above 135F, so cooling methods (moved to the freezer, stirring, ice wands) were implemented. Ice baths were also discussed. Ensure food temperatures are monitored throughout the cooling process to see that foods are cooled from 135F to 70F within 2 hours, and reach 41F within no more than 6 hours total.
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Foods were observed stored directly on the floor of both walk-in freezers. Store foods at least 6 inches above the ground.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Interior of the lower doors on the cookline prep cooler observed to have horizontal gashes. Repair so that doors are smooth and easily cleanable. (Previously observed on 10/11/23 and 4/17/23.)
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Chlorine test strips could not be located to check the dish machine sanitizer concentration. Ensure test strips are available for any sanitizers used.
4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Black soil accumulation was observed in the gaskets of the under-counter freezer on the cookline. Maintain non-food contact surfaces clean.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Dust accumulation observed on racks hanging from the ceiling over the cookline. Clean to eliminate dust accumulation. (Previously observed 10/11/23.)
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: The wall under the 3 compartment sink has been patched but is still not smooth or easily cleanable. Finish patch repair so that the wall is smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation was observed in the kitchen under dry storage shelving and between equipment and the wall. Clean physical facilities as often as needed to keep them clean.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Only one current food handler certificate was available for kitchen employees working during this inspection. Ensure employees complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew as needed. Keep food handler certificates on file for review during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: PIC present has not completed allergen training. Ensure CFMs have ANSI-approved allergen training certificates. (Previously observed on 10/11/23 and 4/17/23.)
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]
